corrections.newExplanation: Cavitating nodules in a profoundly neutropenic AML patient suggest invasive aspergillosis. Serum galactomannan is an Aspergillus-specific antigen test, and a positive result is a mycological criterion for probable invasive aspergillosis that supports starting mould-active therapy such as voriconazole. Beta-D-glucan is pan-fungal and less specific. Sputum Candida culture usually reflects colonisation, and blood cultures rarely grow moulds. Source: IDSA 2016 aspergillosis guideline (Patterson et al, Clin Infect Dis 2016); EORTC/MSGERC 2019 definitions

corrections.newExplanation: In patients on haemodialysis, isoniazid and rifampicin are cleared mainly by the liver, so their doses don't need adjusting for renal failure. People with ESRD are at high risk of isoniazid-related peripheral neuropathy, though, and pyridoxine (vitamin B6) should be co-prescribed with isoniazid. Forgetting pyridoxine is the real pitfall here. Antibiotic lock solutions and in-line filters play no part in oral LTBI treatment. Source: CDC/ATS/IDSA TB treatment guideline (Nahid et al, Clin Infect Dis 2016); NTCA/CDC 2020 LTBI guidelines

corrections.notes: The established absolute contraindication in portopulmonary hypertension is mPAP of 50 mmHg or more (AASLD/ILTS). 'PVR above 8 Wood units' isn't a standard cut-off.
corrections.source: ILTS 2016 portopulmonary hypertension practice guideline (Krowka et al, Transplantation 2016); AASLD 2013 liver transplant evaluation guideline
corrections.newExplanation: In portopulmonary hypertension, mean pulmonary arterial pressure is the key haemodynamic gatekeeper for liver transplantation. An mPAP of 50 mmHg or more is an absolute contraindication because perioperative mortality is very high. Patients with an mPAP of 35 to 50 mmHg need pulmonary vasodilator therapy and may proceed if their haemodynamics improve. PVR and cardiac index help characterise the disease, but a PVR above 8 Wood units isn't a standard listing cut-off. Source: ILTS 2016 portopulmonary hypertension practice guideline (Krowka et al, Transplantation 2016); AASLD 2013 liver transplant evaluation guideline

GINA (since 2019) and the 2024 BTS/NICE/SIGN guideline recommend as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol as the anti-inflammatory reliever for newly diagnosed adults, with review of control and inhaler technique. Source: GINA 2024 strategy report; BTS/NICE/SIGN NG245 asthma guideline (2024)

optionEdits.after: Diagnose asthma and start as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (anti-inflammatory reliever), with follow-up review

corrections.notes: Atovaquone-proguanil is continued for 7 days after leaving the malarious area, not 1 day.
corrections.source: UKHSA ACMP guidelines for malaria prevention in travellers from the UK 2024; CDC Yellow Book
corrections.newExplanation: Atovaquone-proguanil acts on the liver stage of the parasite as well as the blood stage. That's why it is taken for 1 to 2 days before travel, daily while in the malarious area, and for only 7 days after leaving. Mefloquine and doxycycline act only on the blood stage and must be continued for 4 weeks after return. Stopping after 1 day would leave the traveller unprotected. Source: UKHSA ACMP guidelines for malaria prevention in travellers from the UK 2024; CDC Yellow Book

corrections.notes: With total testosterone repeatedly in the borderline 8-12 nmol/L range, EAU and EAA recommend measuring free testosterone and SHBG before deciding on TRT. A third total testosterone isn't required.
corrections.source: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health 2025; BSSM 2023 adult testosterone deficiency guideline
corrections.newExplanation: Two early-morning fasting total testosterone results of 8.8 and 9.5 nmol/L fall in the borderline range (about 8 to 12 nmol/L). Here, guidelines recommend measuring SHBG and calculating free testosterone before deciding on treatment, because altered SHBG can make total testosterone misleading. A third total testosterone wouldn't add useful information. Treating erectile dysfunction alone would ignore possible testosterone deficiency. Source: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health 2025; BSSM 2023 adult testosterone deficiency guideline

corrections.notes: EAU guidelines use a total testosterone threshold of 12.1 nmol/L to diagnose hypogonadism in symptomatic men, not 8 nmol/L.
corrections.source: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health 2025
corrections.newExplanation: The EAU uses a total testosterone threshold of 12.1 nmol/L (350 ng/dL). Below this, symptomatic men have biochemical evidence of hypogonadism that warrants further assessment, including free testosterone where SHBG may be abnormal, and consideration of treatment. 8 nmol/L isn't the EAU diagnostic cut-off. Values that low simply make testosterone deficiency more certain. This man's levels of about 7 nmol/L are well below the threshold. Source: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health 2025

corrections.notes: ESC 2019 recommends systemic thrombolysis (Class I) as first-line for high-risk PE. Surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed therapy is for when thrombolysis is contraindicated or fails, so 'all equally first-line' is incorrect.
corrections.source: ESC 2019 acute pulmonary embolism guideline (Konstantinides et al, Eur Heart J 2020)
corrections.newExplanation: For high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE, ESC 2019 recommends systemic thrombolytic therapy as first-line treatment (class I), alongside unfractionated heparin. Surgical embolectomy or percutaneous catheter-directed treatment is recommended when thrombolysis is contraindicated or has failed. These options aren't equivalent first-line choices. Anticoagulation alone isn't enough for massive PE, and DOACs aren't used in unstable patients. Source: ESC 2019 acute pulmonary embolism guideline (Konstantinides et al, Eur Heart J 2020)

corrections.notes: SSC 2021 recommends an initial MAP target of 65 mmHg over higher targets, including in chronic hypertension (SEPSISPAM showed no mortality benefit).
corrections.source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 (Evans et al, Crit Care Med 2021); SEPSISPAM (Asfar et al, NEJM 2014)
corrections.newExplanation: SSC 2021 recommends an initial mean arterial pressure target of 65 mmHg rather than higher targets in adults with septic shock on vasopressors. SEPSISPAM compared 80 to 85 with 65 to 70 mmHg and found no mortality benefit. In the chronic hypertension subgroup, the higher target reduced renal replacement therapy, but it caused more atrial fibrillation. The 65 trial also found no harm from permissive targets in older patients. Routine individual targets aren't recommended. Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 (Evans et al, Crit Care Med 2021); SEPSISPAM (Asfar et al, NEJM 2014)

corrections.notes: SSC 2021 doesn't recommend raising the MAP target for persistent hypoperfusion. The approach is to keep 65 mmHg and optimise other resuscitation parameters (fluids guided by dynamic measures, CRT, lactate).
corrections.source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 (Evans et al, Crit Care Med 2021)
corrections.newExplanation: If perfusion is still poor once the MAP reaches 65 mmHg, SSC 2021 doesn't advise routinely raising the MAP target. Instead, reassess and optimise the whole resuscitation: fluid responsiveness using dynamic measures, capillary refill time, lactate trend, cardiac function (with consideration of inotropes for low cardiac output), and source control. Giving fluids alone, without assessing responsiveness, risks fluid overload. Source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 (Evans et al, Crit Care Med 2021)

corrections.notes: ESUR 2018 and the ACR Manual on Contrast Media say metformin can continue normally when eGFR ≥30 and there's no AKI. Routine withholding for moderate renal impairment isn't recommended.
corrections.source: ESUR Contrast Media Safety Committee guideline 2018; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023
corrections.newExplanation: Patients with an eGFR of 30 or more and no AKI can keep taking metformin as normal around iodinated contrast. ESUR 2018 and the ACR say routine withholding isn't needed, because contrast-associated lactic acidosis is very rare in this group. Metformin is stopped at the time of contrast, and restarted after 48 hours if renal function is stable, only when the eGFR is below 30, there is AKI, or contrast is given intra-arterially with first-pass renal exposure. Source: ESUR Contrast Media Safety Committee guideline 2018; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2023

corrections.notes: BSR 2022 shortened the methotrexate washout before conception to 1 month (ACR 2020: 1-3 months). '3 months' is outdated, though B is still the best option once reworded.
corrections.source: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (Russell et al, Rheumatology 2023); ACR 2020 reproductive health guideline
corrections.newExplanation: Methotrexate is teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy. The BSR 2022 guideline advises stopping it at least 1 month before conception (ACR 2020 says 1 to 3 months), continuing folic acid, and switching to a pregnancy-compatible drug such as hydroxychloroquine or sulfasalazine to keep the arthritis controlled. Methotrexate's use for ectopic pregnancy reflects its abortifacient effect, which is why it is unsafe in a continuing pregnancy. Source: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (Russell et al, Rheumatology 2023); ACR 2020 reproductive health guideline

optionEdits.after: Methotrexate should be discontinued at least 1 month before attempting conception

corrections.notes: After a first remission, AGA 2016 and UEG/EMCG 2021 advise stopping budesonide and monitoring. Low-dose maintenance is for disease that recurs after stopping.
corrections.source: AGA 2016 microscopic colitis guideline (Nguyen et al, Gastroenterology 2016); UEG/EMCG 2021 European guidelines on microscopic colitis
corrections.newExplanation: Budesonide 9 mg daily is first-line induction for microscopic colitis. Once clinical remission is reached, guidelines advise stopping budesonide and watching for recurrence. Low-dose maintenance budesonide (about 6 mg daily or less) is reserved for patients who relapse after stopping. Azathioprine is for budesonide-refractory or budesonide-dependent disease. Systemic glucocorticoids such as prednisolone are less effective and more toxic, so they aren't used for maintenance. Source: AGA 2016 microscopic colitis guideline (Nguyen et al, Gastroenterology 2016); UEG/EMCG 2021 European guidelines on microscopic colitis

corrections.notes: MGUS progression risk is mainly determined by M-protein level, isotype and FLC ratio (Mayo/IMWG risk model). BMI is a minor association, so A is the most accurate answer.
corrections.source: Kyle et al, long-term follow-up of MGUS (NEJM 2018); Rajkumar et al, Mayo MGUS risk model (Blood 2005); IMWG 2010 MGUS guidelines
corrections.newExplanation: MGUS progresses to myeloma or a related disorder at about 1% per year. The main predictors are the size of the M-protein, a non-IgG isotype, an abnormal serum free light chain ratio, and a higher bone marrow plasma cell percentage. Obesity has been associated with a slightly higher risk, but it isn't a major predictor. Risk is never negligible, and patients need lifelong risk-adapted follow-up even without symptoms. Source: Kyle et al, long-term follow-up of MGUS (NEJM 2018); Rajkumar et al, Mayo MGUS risk model (Blood 2005); IMWG 2010 MGUS guidelines

corrections.notes: PERSEUS (NEJM 2024) made D-VRd quadruplet induction the standard for transplant-eligible NDMM (NCCN/EHA-EMN 2025). RVd triplet is outdated.
corrections.source: Sonneveld et al, PERSEUS (NEJM 2024); NCCN Multiple Myeloma guideline 2025; EHA-EMN 2025 guideline
corrections.newExplanation: In PERSEUS, adding daratumumab to VRd induction and consolidation, followed by daratumumab-lenalidomide maintenance, significantly improved progression-free survival and MRD negativity over VRd in transplant-eligible newly diagnosed myeloma. Quadruplet anti-CD38-based induction such as D-VRd is now the preferred standard (NCCN, EHA-EMN 2025). VCd is mainly used when renal impairment or access issues apply. DVd and KRd aren't standard induction regimens. Source: Sonneveld et al, PERSEUS (NEJM 2024); NCCN Multiple Myeloma guideline 2025; EHA-EMN 2025 guideline

optionEdits.after: Daratumumab plus lenalidomide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (D-VRd)

corrections.notes: Natalizumab doesn't meaningfully impair COVID-19 vaccine humoral responses. Blunted responses are seen with anti-CD20 agents and S1P modulators, so B is correct.
corrections.source: Achiron et al, humoral response to BNT162b2 in MS patients on DMTs (Ther Adv Neurol Disord 2021); Sormani et al, Lancet eBioMedicine 2021
corrections.newExplanation: Antibody responses to COVID-19 vaccines are broadly preserved in people with MS on natalizumab, and are similar to untreated patients and healthy controls. Markedly blunted humoral responses occur mainly with anti-CD20 therapies (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, rituximab) and S1P receptor modulators (fingolimod and others). In those patients, vaccine timing and extra doses matter. Natalizumab doesn't enhance immunogenicity. Source: Achiron et al, humoral response to BNT162b2 in MS patients on DMTs (Ther Adv Neurol Disord 2021); Sormani et al, Lancet eBioMedicine 2021

corrections.notes: Under the current ATS/IDSA 2007 criteria, kept in the 2020 ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA guideline, two positive sputum cultures meet the microbiological criterion. The keyed answer applies superseded 1997 criteria.
corrections.source: Griffith et al, ATS/IDSA 2007 NTM statement; Daley et al, ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA 2020 NTM guideline
corrections.newExplanation: Under the ATS/IDSA criteria (kept in the 2020 guideline), the microbiological criterion is met by positive cultures from at least two separate expectorated sputum samples, whatever the smear result. This patient also has symptoms and a new infiltrate, and needs other diagnoses reasonably excluded. So he meets the diagnostic criteria for NTM lung disease. Lung biopsy is only needed when sputum doesn't meet the criteria. Source: Griffith et al, ATS/IDSA 2007 NTM statement; Daley et al, ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA 2020 NTM guideline

corrections.notes: EULAR 2023 defines erosive hand OA by radiographic erosions, so it can't be diagnosed 'without erosions'. Genetic testing has no role in routine hand OA diagnosis, so D is correct.
corrections.source: EULAR 2018 hand OA management recommendations (Kloppenburg et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019); EULAR 2023 hand OA classification criteria
corrections.newExplanation: Hand osteoarthritis is diagnosed clinically, using typical symptoms and signs such as Heberden and Bouchard nodes, plus radiographs when needed. Genetic testing has no role in routine diagnosis or management. Erosive hand OA is defined by central erosions on radiographs, so it can't be labelled erosive without them. Nodes don't exclude a genetic predisposition, since hand OA is strongly heritable, and they don't mean the disease is stable. Source: EULAR 2018 hand OA management recommendations (Kloppenburg et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2019); EULAR 2023 hand OA classification criteria

corrections.notes: In suspected PJI, IDSA 2013 recommends diagnostic joint aspiration (cell count, differential, culture) before antibiotics. Bone biopsy is not the first step.
corrections.source: IDSA 2013 prosthetic joint infection guideline (Osmon et al, Clin Infect Dis 2013); 2018 ICM PJI criteria
corrections.newExplanation: In suspected prosthetic joint infection, IDSA recommends diagnostic arthrocentesis before antibiotics in a stable patient. Send the synovial fluid for total cell count, differential and culture. Antibiotics should ideally be held for at least 2 weeks before sampling to improve culture yield. Bone biopsy isn't the first step, and empiric antibiotics before aspiration reduce the chance of identifying the organism. CRP and ESR support the diagnosis but don't identify the pathogen. Source: IDSA 2013 prosthetic joint infection guideline (Osmon et al, Clin Infect Dis 2013); 2018 ICM PJI criteria

corrections.notes: NCCN recommends germline testing for everyone with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, whatever the family history, so immediate testing (B) is correct, not counselling first.
corrections.source: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma guideline (JNCCN 2021); ASCO 2019 provisional clinical opinion (Stoffel et al, J Clin Oncol 2019)
corrections.newExplanation: NCCN and ASCO recommend germline genetic testing for everyone diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, whatever their family history. This is because many carriers of pathogenic variants (for example BRCA1/2, PALB2 or ATM) don't have a suggestive family history, and results can guide treatment such as platinum chemotherapy and olaparib maintenance. Testing shouldn't wait for a detailed pedigree. Genetic counselling can be offered alongside it. Source: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma guideline (JNCCN 2021); ASCO 2019 provisional clinical opinion (Stoffel et al, J Clin Oncol 2019)

corrections.notes: ENETS 2023 and ESMO 2020 recommend active surveillance for asymptomatic, non-functioning G1 PanNETs of 2 cm or less, with the first imaging at about 6 months. Routine resection at 1.5 cm isn't recommended.
corrections.source: ENETS 2023 guidance for non-functioning PanNET (Kos-Kudla et al, J Neuroendocrinol 2023); ESMO GEP-NEN guideline 2020
corrections.newExplanation: For asymptomatic, non-functioning, well-differentiated G1 pancreatic NETs of 2 cm or less without suspicious features, ENETS and ESMO recommend active surveillance rather than routine resection. Repeat imaging at about 6 months, then annually if the tumour is stable. Pancreatic surgery carries substantial morbidity, and these tumours rarely progress. Somatostatin analogues and chemotherapy aren't indicated for small, low-grade incidental tumours. Source: ENETS 2023 guidance for non-functioning PanNET (Kos-Kudla et al, J Neuroendocrinol 2023); ESMO GEP-NEN guideline 2020

corrections.notes: Anti-Hu is a high-risk antibody (more than 85% cancer, mostly SCLC). Updated PNS criteria and EFNS call for prompt tumour screening, so D is correct.
corrections.source: Graus et al, updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021); EFNS 2011 tumour screening guideline
corrections.newExplanation: Anti-Hu is a high-risk paraneoplastic antibody: more than 85% of patients have a cancer, most often small cell lung cancer. With a compatible syndrome, the priority is prompt tumour screening with CT chest, then FDG-PET if that is negative. Treating the tumour is the main way to stabilise the neurological disease. Waiting for CSF results or repeating the antibody test delays diagnosis. Immunotherapy may be added, but it doesn't replace the tumour search. Source: Graus et al, updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021); EFNS 2011 tumour screening guideline

corrections.notes: Current UK (Association of Anaesthetists et al 2025) and US multisociety (2024) guidance no longer advise routinely stopping GLP-1 RAs before surgery. They continue them with individual aspiration-risk assessment.
corrections.source: Association of Anaesthetists/CPOC/ABCD multisociety guidance on GLP-1 and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists (Anaesthesia 2025); ASA/AGA/ASMBS/ISPOR/SAGES multisociety guidance 2024
corrections.newExplanation: Earlier advice (ASA 2023) was to withhold weekly GLP-1 receptor agonists for a week before elective surgery. Current UK (2025) and US multisociety (2024) guidance no longer recommends routine withholding, because that disrupts glycaemic control and the evidence of harm is limited. GLP-1 RAs are generally continued. Patients at higher aspiration risk, for example in the dose-escalation phase or with GI symptoms, are managed with a liquid diet beforehand or a rapid-sequence approach. Source: Association of Anaesthetists/CPOC/ABCD multisociety guidance on GLP-1 and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists (Anaesthesia 2025); ASA/AGA/ASMBS/ISPOR/SAGES multisociety guidance 2024

corrections.notes: ISPD 2022: repeat peritonitis with different organisms is treated with empirical IP antibiotics. The catheter is removed for refractory (not clear by day 5), relapsing or fungal peritonitis, not automatically for a third episode.
corrections.source: ISPD peritonitis recommendations 2022 update (Li PK et al, Perit Dial Int 2022)
corrections.newExplanation: This is a repeat peritonitis episode (different organisms each time), not a relapsing or refractory one. ISPD 2022 recommends starting empirical intraperitoneal antibiotics covering Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms, then tailoring them to culture, while monitoring the clinical response. Catheter removal is indicated for refractory peritonitis (effluent not clearing after 5 days of appropriate antibiotics), relapsing peritonitis, or fungal peritonitis. A third episode alone isn't an indication. Source: ISPD peritonitis recommendations 2022 update (Li PK et al, Perit Dial Int 2022)

corrections.notes: The key's own explanation says PMN 210 is below the 250 threshold, so option C ('diagnostic') contradicts it. A is the consistent answer.
corrections.source: EASL 2018 decompensated cirrhosis guideline; AASLD 2021 ascites/SBP guidance
corrections.newExplanation: The ascitic neutrophil (PMN) count is the total white cell count multiplied by the neutrophil fraction: 300 x 0.70 = 210 cells/mm3. SBP is diagnosed when the ascitic PMN count is 250 cells/mm3 or more, so 210 doesn't meet the threshold. Send ascitic fluid cultures in blood culture bottles anyway, because bacterascites can occur below this level. Look for another cause of her encephalopathy, such as GI bleeding, infection elsewhere or electrolyte disturbance. Source: EASL 2018 decompensated cirrhosis guideline; AASLD 2021 ascites/SBP guidance

corrections.notes: Under the Pei unified criteria in KDIGO 2025, at age 15-39 with a family history, 3 or more cysts in total (unilateral or bilateral) is diagnostic. Five cysts at 28 confirms ADPKD.
corrections.source: KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline; Pei et al, unified ultrasound criteria (J Am Soc Nephrol 2009)
corrections.newExplanation: In someone at risk of ADPKD from a family history of unknown genotype, the Pei unified ultrasound criteria apply. Between ages 15 and 39, three or more renal cysts in total (unilateral or bilateral) are diagnostic. This 28-year-old has five cysts, so the findings confirm ADPKD. Genetic testing or MRI is useful when the imaging is equivocal, for example in younger people or potential living donors, but isn't needed here. Source: KDIGO 2025 ADPKD guideline; Pei et al, unified ultrasound criteria (J Am Soc Nephrol 2009)

corrections.notes: The 2024 SVI trial (linked) found rectal indomethacin alone was not inferior to, and had fewer PEP cases than, indomethacin plus pancreatic stent. The combination is no longer preferred.
corrections.source: Elmunzer et al, indomethacin with or without prophylactic pancreatic stent placement (SVI trial, Lancet 2024); ESGE 2019 PEP guideline
corrections.newExplanation: Rectal NSAIDs (indomethacin or diclofenac 100 mg) given immediately before ERCP are recommended for all patients without a contraindication to reduce post-ERCP pancreatitis. In high-risk patients, the 2024 SVI trial found rectal indomethacin alone non-inferior to, and associated with fewer PEP cases than, indomethacin plus a prophylactic pancreatic stent. So routinely adding a stent is no longer needed. IV lactated Ringer's can be an adjunct but isn't the main measure. Source: Elmunzer et al, indomethacin with or without prophylactic pancreatic stent placement (SVI trial, Lancet 2024); ESGE 2019 PEP guideline

corrections.notes: Paediatric PEP should be a three-drug regimen. BHIVA/BASHH 2021 uses tenofovir/emtricitabine plus raltegravir, and CDC 2025 prefers an INSTI plus two NRTIs. Dual raltegravir plus tenofovir isn't recommended.
corrections.source: BHIVA/BASHH UK guideline for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis 2021; CDC nPEP guidelines 2025
corrections.newExplanation: HIV PEP should be a three-drug regimen. For children, BHIVA/BASHH and CDC recommend two NRTIs plus an integrase inhibitor, such as tenofovir disoproxil/emtricitabine plus raltegravir, dosed for weight and age, for 28 days. Dual therapy (raltegravir plus tenofovir, or tenofovir/emtricitabine alone) isn't recommended for PEP. Lopinavir/ritonavir-based regimens are poorly tolerated, and zidovudine monotherapy is obsolete. Source: BHIVA/BASHH UK guideline for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis 2021; CDC nPEP guidelines 2025
